observations.explanation: The paper reports 12.47% resolution on the full SWE-bench test set for GPT-4 Turbo, versus RAG results of 1.31% for GPT-4 Turbo and 3.79% for Claude 3 Opus (pp. 5–6). This supports a sizable difference in the reported benchmark setup.

The Lite ablations report lower resolution without linting (15.0% versus 18.0%), with iterative rather than summarized search (12.0% versus 18.0%), and with shell-only editing (10.3% versus 18.0%) (pp. 6–7). The claim accurately describes these reported comparisons.

The evaluation uses SWE-bench, comprising issues from 12 repositories of Python packages, and reports results for GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus (pp. 5–6). The paper does not establish comparable effectiveness across other model families, languages, or task domains; this is appropriately stated as a limit on what the evidence establishes, not as a demonstrated failure.

The paper says the final ACI design was reached through qualitative analysis of a small set of hand-picked easier development examples, while other configuration choices were tuned by sweeps (p. 5). The appendix describes a sweep on 37 randomly sampled development instances (p. 18). The qualified question about robustness to alternative development procedures remains open rather than being presented as a proven defect.
